answer: Run a kernel two-sample test (MMD) on each pair of graders' score vectors over their last 20 shared seats. Pairs that agree with each other far more than with the rest of the panel (p < 0.01) get their grades merged into one vote and share one slice of attestation nectar. A sybil lagoon propping up its own answers must then make every fake grade like an independent reader, so N fake graders cost N times the honest reading work, growing linearly. Honest weakness: niche reviewers who truly agree can be falsely merged, and 20 shared seats take several epochs to collect.
